See also form,<br>customer, inventory item, and inventory.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| attribute class      | A grouping of your company's leads, opportunities, customers, or cases by a<br>specific set of attributes. See also attribute.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| authentication       | The process by which establishes a potential user as valid and grants access to<br>the system. A user must use a valid username and password pair for successful<br>authentication. See also user.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| authorization        | The process by which verifies whether a user has sufficient access rights to<br>particular forms, elements, and actions. The system makes this determina<br>tion for a user who has successfully signed in, based on the roles assigned to<br>the user and the restriction groups that include the user as a member. See also<br>user, form, role, and restriction group.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| auto-reversing batch | A batch for which the system automatically creates another batch that revers<br>es debit and credit entries into the next financial period; the debit entry is re<br>versed as a credit entry and vice versa. Auto-reversing entries are used to re<br>verse some period-end adjustments. See also batch, general ledger, and finan<br>cial period.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| automation schedule  | A schedule defined for an processing form to direct the system to perform spe<br>cific processing periodically. You can create automation schedules by using<br>the Automation Schedules (SM205020) form. See also automation schedule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| B                    |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| bank account         | A cash account associated with a specific bank (which in is defined as a ven<br>dor) and with one or more linked clearing accounts. Bank charges can be con<br>figured as entry types associated with the bank account. Bank accounts gener<br>ally require periodic reconciliations to be performed. See also vendor, clearing<br>account, entry type, and reconciliation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| base currency        | The currency of the environment in which the company generates and ex<br>pends cash. A base currency can be the only currency used in the system or<br>one of multiple currencies used. The base currency is the default currency for<br>recording transactions, budgets, and other GL data, and it is used for report<br>ing, income statement, and balance sheet calculations. For general ledger ac<br>counts denominated to a foreign currency, maintains the history of transac<br>tions and balances in both the currency of denomination and the base curren<br>cy. See also general ledger and account. |

<span id="page-192-4"></span><span id="page-192-3"></span><span id="page-192-2"></span><span id="page-192-1"></span><span id="page-192-0"></span>

| base price              | A price for an item set with respect to the base unit, expressed in the base cur<br>rency and offered to customers of the base price class (those not associated<br>with any specific price class by default). Base prices can be defined and main<br>tained directly, following your company's pricing policy. See also base unit,<br>base currency, customer, and inventory.                                                                                                                                                                        |
|-------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| base unit               | The unit of measure in which a particular item is tracked from the moment it is<br>received at a warehouse or produced at one of your facilities until it is picked<br>for shipping. Generally, the base unit is the smallest unit defined in the system<br>for a particular item. Also, the base unit is the unit of measure used for calcu<br>lating item costs. See also warehouse.                                                                                                                                                                |
| batch                   | A set of related transactions or journal entries that are in the same currency,<br>refer to the same ledger, and occur in the same financial period. A batch's deb<br>it total and credit total are calculated over all the transactions. Some batches<br>are generated by the system automatically, such as those implementing reval<br>uations. Only balanced batches (those for which the credit total equals the<br>debit total) can be released and posted to the specified ledger. See also journal<br>entry, financial period, and revaluation |
| batch control total     | A user-entered total that is used for batch status validation if it is enforced<br>in your system—that is, if theValidate Batch ControlTotals on Entry check<br>box on the General Ledger Preferences (GL102000) is selected. A batch can be<br>saved with the Balanced status only if the user types into this box a value that<br>is equal to the batch's debit total and credit total amounts. We recommend<br>that you use batch control total validation to reduce data input errors. See al<br>so batch.                                        |
| budget article          | An account-subaccount pair recorded in a budget ledger with a budget<br>amount. A budget article has subarticles if its subaccount has at least one ag<br>gregating value in any segment. See also account, subaccount, aggregating val<br>ue, and segment.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| business account        | A set of information about one of your company's vendors or customers, in<br>cluding its locations, contacts, and payment and shipping options. Acumatica<br>ERP uses this information, which is specified on data entry forms, throughout<br>the system. Your company also has a business account to record its own loca<br>tions, contacts, and shipping settings. See also vendor, customer, and location.                                                                                                                                         |
| C                       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| cash account            | A special type of general ledger account used to record various monetary<br>transactions in a specific currency. You can specify entry types and payment<br>methods with which the cash account is associated. Each cash account is as<br>signed to a specific branch. See also general ledger, account, entry type, pay<br>ment method.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| cash-in-transit account | An account used for cash that is being moved from one currency to another.<br>Because cross-rates are not used in Acumatica ERP, currency conversion is<br>performed via the base currency with the use of the cash-in-transit account<br>and subaccount. See also account, base currency, and subaccount.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

<span id="page-193-5"></span><span id="page-193-4"></span><span id="page-193-3"></span><span id="page-193-2"></span><span id="page-193-1"></span><span id="page-193-0"></span>

| cash discount       | A deduction from the total payable amount, which is allowed if the amount<br>owed is paid within a specified time period on or before a due date. Cash dis<br>counts available for your organization are defined by credit terms assigned<br>to vendors, and cash discounts available for customers are defined by credit<br>terms assigned to customers. See also credit terms, vendor, and customer                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|---------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| cash management     | A functional area of Acumatica ERP that you use to manage cash and bank ac<br>counts, cash transactions (including funds transfer), and bank statement rec<br>onciliations. See also cash account, bank account, funds transfer, and reconcilia<br>tion.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| chart of accounts   | A listing of the accounts in the system to which you will record accounting<br>transactions. The chart of accounts, which you maintain in Acumatica ERP<br>by using the Chart of Accounts (GL202500) form, consists of balance sheet ac<br>counts (assets and liabilities) and income statement accounts (income and ex<br>penses). The chart of accounts should follow national and industry standards<br>while also reflecting the operations of your company. See also account.                                                                                                                                      |
| clearing account    | A cash account that temporarily holds customer payments included in a de<br>posit. Once the money is actually deposited to the bank and the deposit is<br>released, a batch of transactions will be generated to move the payment<br>amounts from clearing accounts to the bank account and to record the<br>charges incurred as expenses. See also cash account, customer, deposit, batch,<br>and bank account.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| combined subaccount | A subaccount that can be combined from multiple involved subaccounts,<br>based on rules you create, for certain transactions; use elements with labels<br>such as CombineSubaccount From to set up these rules. A box for a com<br>bined subaccount displays a subaccount mask, such as ––––.––.–––.––––, in<br>accordance with the segmented structure of subaccounts defined for your<br>company. For each segment, you can specify one of the involved subaccounts<br>as the source of the segment value. See the Combined Subaccounts article for<br>more information. See also subaccount and combined subaccount. |
| commission          | A payment made to a salesperson for goods and services sold. Commission<br>is calculated once in a commission period based on total invoice amounts or<br>payments received, depending on your configuration choice. For each docu<br>ment, calculates the commission amount as a percentage. For an invoice, the<br>commission may be split among multiple salespeople.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| common settings     | A functional area of Acumatica ERP used by administrators and implementa<br>tion consultants to control global system settings. Some configuration set<br>tings—such as company information, segmented keys, and numbering se<br>quences—must be provided during initial system setup and cannot be mod<br>ified later. Other information, such as credit terms and logistics settings, can<br>be added at any time. See also segmented key, numbering sequence, and credit<br>terms.                                                                                                                                   |
| consolidation       | The process of combining separate accounting data into one set of data by im<br>porting data from subsidiaries to the parent company. Whether your organiza<br>tion is a parent company or a subsidiary of a larger company, you can prepare<br>and consolidate the data into one consolidation ledger in the parent company.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| consolidation data  | The data imported to the parent company (as GL batches with system-gener<br>ated descriptions) to enable consolidation. See also general ledger, batch, and<br>consolidation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

<span id="page-194-5"></span><span id="page-194-4"></span><span id="page-194-3"></span><span id="page-194-2"></span><span id="page-194-1"></span><span id="page-194-0"></span>

| consolidation mapping | The process of matching accounts and subaccounts in a subsidiary against<br>those of the parent company for consolidation. Mapping of subaccounts can<br>be performed across subaccount segments. See also account, subaccount, and<br>segment.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|-----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| credit terms          | Conditions and stipulations used by vendors in their relations with your com<br>pany and by your company in its relations with customers when any outstand<br>ing balance is paid. Credit terms include an installment option (one payment<br>or multiple installments), a payment schedule, and terms for cash discount<br>(for only the single-installment option). Also, credit terms can be used as a<br>schedule for overdue charges. See also vendor, customer, cash discount, and<br>credit terms.                                                                        |
| currency management   | A functional area of Acumatica ERP that you use to define multiple currencies,<br>enabling foreign currency transactions throughout the system. You can main<br>tain the lists of currencies, track exchange rate fluctuations, and perform peri<br>odical revaluations. See also revaluation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| currency rate         | The rating of one currency valued against another. You use the Currency Rates<br>(CM301000) form to enter foreign currencies' exchange rates and the base cur<br>rency rates. Rates for each rate type are specified with respect to the base cur<br>rency and are recorded to the database with the type of arithmetic operation<br>required to apply the rate. Each record contains the rate and the date when it<br>becomes effective. The rate is used for currency conversions for documents<br>that have later dates until a new rate is recorded. See also base currency. |
| customer              | One of your company's trade debtors. In Acumatica ERP, you can set up de<br>fault values for individual customers, customer classes, and customer doc<br>uments to help make data entry easier and less error-prone. When you en<br>ter a new invoice for a customer, calculates the due date, discount date, and<br>amount automatically, based on its credit terms. Tax settings are by default<br>those of the tax zone associated with the customer location. See also customer<br>class, credit terms, tax, and tax zone.                                                   |
| customer class        | A group of settings that provides default values when users create new cus<br>tomer accounts, thus saving them time. You divide customers into classes<br>based on the types of goods or services they purchase from you. See also cus<br>tomer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| customer management   | A functional area of Acumatica ERP that helps your company set up customer<br>service based on contracts and effectively track service issues reported by cus<br>tomers. Also, the functionality provides tools to help salespeople generate<br>quality leads, track and analyze sales opportunities, and manage marketing<br>campaigns by sending personalized emails in bulk. See also customer.                                                                                                                                                                               |
| customer price class  | A group of customers that may be offered special prices because of their buy<br>ing habits. All customers of the same customer price class are charged the<br>same price for the same item, and you can set different prices for the same<br>item for different customer price classes. See also customer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| customer statement    | A complete record of the customer's invoices, debit and credit memos, pay<br>ments, prepayments, and overdue charges for a specific period. A statement<br>includes all new activity for a statement cycle, from the previous statement<br>date to the current statement date. Any open debit items from prior periods<br>are included in the statement, grouped by days outstanding. See also state<br>ment cycle and prepayment.                                                                                                                                               |

<span id="page-195-6"></span><span id="page-195-5"></span><span id="page-195-4"></span><span id="page-195-3"></span><span id="page-195-2"></span><span id="page-195-1"></span><span id="page-195-0"></span>

| dashboard         | An interface that organizes and presents key information in a format that<br>users can interpret easily. System administrators can design a set of compa<br>ny-specific template dashboards. A user can modify any of them or create<br>from scratch a set of personalized dashboards that display information tai<br>lored to job and information needs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|-------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| deferral code     | A code used in Acumatica ERP to configure how revenues and expenses are<br>recognized. If a line amount in an invoice or a bill should be recognized over<br>several periods, a deferral code (of the revenue or expense type, respectively)<br>is assigned to this line.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| deferral schedule | A number of related transactions automatically generated for the documents<br>whose lines have deferral codes assigned. See also deferral code.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| deferred revenue  | A functional area of Acumatica ERP that stores definitions of deferral codes,<br>while giving you the ability to view and edit deferral schedules generated for<br>AP and AR documents and recognize parts of deferred amount according to<br>these schedules.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| deposit           | 1. An instance of physically placing money in a bank.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|                   | 2. In Acumatica ERP, an internal document created using the Bank Deposits<br>(CA305000) form. Batch deposits are used to group customer payments de<br>posited to the bank in bulk. When you enter payments intended for such<br>deposits into Acumatica ERP, they are recorded to special clearing ac<br>counts, which temporarily hold payments drawn from customers' AR ac<br>counts. Before you make a deposit to the bank, you create a deposit in<br>Acumatica ERP, list the payments and cash to be deposited, and print a de<br>posit slip. After the money was actually deposited, the deposit can be cor<br>rected to contain only payments accepted by the bank and released. On<br>the deposit's release, a batch of transactions will be generated to move<br>the payment amounts from clearing accounts to the bank account and to<br>record the charges incurred as expenses.<br>See also deposit, batch, customer, clearing account, and bank account. |
| discount          | A means of reducing sales prices. In Acumatica ERP, your company can config<br>ure various types of discounts applicable to sales orders and intended to at<br>tract customers: document-level discounts that are subtracted from the doc<br>ument total, item-level discounts that apply to a document line, and flat-price<br>discounts, which are special discounted prices that depend on the quantities<br>of goods purchased. See also customer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| E                 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| entry type        | A user-defined type of transaction (which can be a cash receipt or cash dis<br>bursement) used to categorize cash transactions. See also cash management.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| event             | An activity that has a specific start time and duration. You create events for all<br>or several users and invite users, leads, contacts, and customers as attendees.<br>You can send invitation or rescheduling emails to attendees.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| F                 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|                   |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

<span id="page-196-7"></span><span id="page-196-6"></span><span id="page-196-5"></span><span id="page-196-4"></span><span id="page-196-3"></span><span id="page-196-2"></span><span id="page-196-1"></span><span id="page-196-0"></span>

| Favorites                    | Links to the forms the particular user accesses most frequently. Any user can<br>create his or her own list of favorites for personal use.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| financial period             | A part of a financial year defined by its start date and end date. A financial year<br>can be divided into monthly, bimonthly, quarterly, or custom-defined periods.<br>For each next new year, generates financial periods in accordance with initial<br>system settings. We recommend that you not change financial settings in once<br>transactions have been posted to any of the periods. See also financial year.                                                                                                 |
| financial year               | A time interval used for calculating annual financial statements. The year is de<br>fined by its start date, which you determine, and lasts 12 months. For example,<br>the U.S. government's financial year begins on October 1 of the previous cal<br>endar year and ends on September 30 of the year that gives the financial year<br>its number. A financial year consists of a number of financial periods and may<br>include an additional adjustment period. See also financial period and adjust<br>ment period. |
| FOB point                    | A destination at which the vendor delivers the goods to be loaded to the trans<br>portation provided by the carrier. The customer covers the freight and other<br>expenses for the cargo from a FOB (meaning freight on board) point. See also<br>vendor and customer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| foreign currency translation | The process of restating the account balances in a reporting currency. For ac<br>counts denominated to currencies other than the reporting currency, the bal<br>ances expressed in the base currency are recalculated to the reporting curren<br>cy. See also account and base currency.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| form                         | A screen in Acumatica ERP that you use to enter needed data, configure and<br>maintain system functionality, view inquiry data, and perform processes that<br>are key to your business.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| form toolbar                 | A toolbar present on most forms with data navigation and processing buttons<br>to invoke actions that apply to the entire form. For example, its actions can be<br>used to cancel or save changes you've made, to insert or delete objects, or to<br>navigate through the objects created via the form. See also form.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| funds transfer               | A transaction that moves an amount from one cash account to another, with<br>related service charges. Funds can be transferred between accounts denomi<br>nated to different foreign currencies in two steps, using the cash in transit ac<br>count for currency conversion to the base currency and from the base curren<br>cy. See also cash account, cash-in-transit account, and base currency.                                                                                                                     |
| G                            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| general ledger               | A functional area of Acumatica ERP that serves as the central application<br>where all financial information is collected for analyzing, summarizing, and re<br>porting. You can set up your company's financial structure through the chart of<br>accounts and subaccounts, collect information through transactions entered<br>by users, and prepare data for generating various financial statements. See al<br>so chart of accounts and subaccount.                                                                 |
| H                            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

<span id="page-197-6"></span><span id="page-197-5"></span><span id="page-197-4"></span><span id="page-197-3"></span><span id="page-197-2"></span><span id="page-197-1"></span><span id="page-197-0"></span>

| historical rate       | An exchange rate for the foreign currency with respect to the base currency<br>that was effective during a certain past period. The system uses historical rates<br>for foreign currency translations and "past-date" transactions. See also base<br>currency and general ledger.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|-----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| I                     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| inline editor         | An editing tool you can use to edit a section of a Wiki article or its full text. The<br>inline editor contains both a text box (which contains the text of the applicable<br>section) and a Formatting toolbar.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| input mask            | A mask implemented to govern what a user may enter into a box, so that the<br>required format is used on data entry forms. Masks are used, for example, for<br>phone numbers, postal codes, and tax registration IDs. Moreover, input masks<br>can be created using regular expressions to validate entered values, since the<br>values for some elements must follow not only input format requirements but<br>also specific rules.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| integration services  | The powerful capabilities that provide the ability to filter and import data from<br>external sources, converting it into internal format, and configure data syn<br>chronization between and third-party applications to be performed on sched<br>ule. Also, you can configure data export with conversion to required formats.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| inventory item        | A stock or non-stock item defined and tracked in Acumatica ERP. The record's<br>unique identifier, Inventory ID, as with other identifiers in Acumatica ERP, can<br>be segmented, with special meaning assigned to each segment. (The INVEN<br>TORY key is used to configure inventory IDs.) Well-designed inventory IDs can<br>help you sort and group items in operational and management reports. See al<br>so stock item and non-stock item.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| inventory             | A functional area of Acumatica ERP that provides real-time access to item<br>availability data configured in accordance with your company's policies. You<br>can maintain a perpetual inventory system as well as performing physical in<br>ventories, which can be performed as full inventory and by cycles. You can use<br>subitems as an additional means of tracking special types of inventory items,<br>and you can track inventory items by either lot or serial numbers and expira<br>tion dates. (See lot serial numbers for more details.) Advanced inventory func<br>tionality includes flexible posting settings, multiple warehouses with multiple<br>specialized locations, and automatic replenishments. See also subitems, inven<br>tory item, and lot or serial numbers. |
| inventory price class | A class used to group inventory items by the method of their price calculation.<br>An inventory price class may include items of one or more item classes. See al<br>so inventory item and item class.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| item class            | A class used to group stock or non-stock items with similar properties and to<br>provide default settings for new items. See also stock item and non-stock item.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| J                     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

<span id="page-198-4"></span><span id="page-198-3"></span><span id="page-198-2"></span><span id="page-198-1"></span><span id="page-198-0"></span>

| journal entry         | A record of debit or credit to any account in the general ledger. Journal en<br>tries (or transactions), which are added in batches, must follow the general<br>ized double-entry rule: the debit total must be equal to the credit total through<br>all the entries in a batch. The batch contains the date, the accounts and sub<br>accounts to be debited, the accounts and subaccounts to be credited, and the<br>debit or credit amounts for each transaction. A batch of journal entries can be<br>marked as recurring or auto-reversing. See also account, general ledger, batch,<br>subaccount, and auto-reversing batch.                                                     |
|-----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| K                     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| kit                   | An inventory item that consists of other stock or non-stock items as compo<br>nents and requires assembling (or packaging) to become a salable good. You<br>enter a kit as a stock or non-stock item using either the Stock Items (IN202500)<br>or Non-Stock Items (IN202000) form and select the Is a Kit option. You can<br>specify the kit's components (with their quantities) using the Kit Specifications<br>(IN209500) form. A kit may include a number of stock and non-stock compo<br>nents. See also inventory item, non-stock item, and stock item.                                                                                                                        |
| L                     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| landed costs          | All extra costs—beyond the prices at which the goods are purchased from ven<br>dors—associated with acquiring products and "landing" them at one of your<br>company's locations. These costs might include customs duties, handling<br>fees, freight charges, value-added taxes, and other costs for a particular prod<br>uct. In Acumatica ERP, you can define these costs via the Landed Cost Codes<br>(PO202000) form. See also vendor and tax.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| location              | 1. One of multiple places of business for a particular company. Each location<br>is assigned to a tax zone and, as a business entity, may have a separate tax<br>registration ID from that of the main location of the company.<br>2. A warehouse location.<br>See also tax zone and warehouse location.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| location table        | The list of a particular warehouse's locations and their properties. Use the lo<br>cation table to configure your warehouse to fit the logistical processes estab<br>lished in your company. For each location table, you can specify whether to<br>include the quantities of stock items stored at this location in the quantity of<br>available items calculated for the warehouse, whether to cost the inventory<br>on this location separately, what inventory operations are allowed for the lo<br>cation, and what the location's pick priority is. Users can consult this table for<br>reference when they're creating receipts, issues, or transfers. See also ware<br>house. |
| lot or serial numbers | Identifying numbers through which you track goods in your inventory. Serial<br>numbers are used when you need to trace each item of the same inventory ID,<br>while lot numbers are used to trace items (of the same ID) that were purchased<br>or produced together and have the same expiration dates (if applicable). You<br>can segment lot and serial numbers by using the Lot/Serial Classes (IN207000)<br>form. Acumatica ERP supports the following types of segments for lot/serial<br>numbers: constant, date, and auto-incrementing. See also segment.                                                                                                                     |

<span id="page-199-2"></span><span id="page-199-1"></span><span id="page-199-0"></span>

| low seasons           | Time intervals in which the decreasing factors (used to divide the standard re<br>plenishment quantity to get lower replenishment quantities during low sea<br>sons) should be applied to quantities on purchase orders generated to replen<br>ish the stock. Each inventory item may have multiple low seasons, each with<br>different decreasing factors. See also inventory item.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|-----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| M                     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| main menu             | A panel located on the le side of the Acumatica ERP screen that contains<br>the links to your favorites and workspaces (menus with links to forms and re<br>ports). See also form, Favorites, and dashboard                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| management            | A functional area of Acumatica ERP that you use to define users, roles, and re<br>striction groups for security management. It also provides site management,<br>wiki management, task management, customization management, and file<br>management capabilities, as well as integration services. See also user, role,<br>restriction group, and integration services.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| multicurrency         | A mode in which Acumatica ERP can function to support multiple currencies.<br>If you have activated multicurrency support, you can manage transactions in<br>various foreign currencies, record exchange rates for multiple rate types as<br>needed, report in a specific foreign currency, and revalue GL, AP, and AR ac<br>counts in the base currency. The base currency is used for reporting and in<br>come statement calculation. See also base currency and Currency Manage<br>ment.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| N                     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| negative inventory    | An option, offered in Acumatica ERP, allowing a negative inventory balance for<br>an inventory item or a group of items. This can occur when the inventory issue<br>is made before the necessary quantity of the item arrives at the warehouse. To<br>calculate the balance of over-issued inventory items, the most recent histori<br>cal cost will be used until the item is received. When the inventory is received,<br>the system will match the receipt cost with the issue cost, and generate a cost<br>adjustment for the difference. Appropriate warnings are issued on transac<br>tions that will result in negative inventory balances. See also inventory item and<br>warehouse. |
| non-stock item        | An inventory item that is not stored in a warehouse. Such items can be of dif<br>ferent types: labor, service (such as product assembly, installation, or person<br>alization), charge, expense, and actual non-stock items, such as goods used<br>only for drop-shipments. For a non-stock item, you can specify the following<br>information in Acumatica ERP: base, sales, and purchase units; conversion co<br>efficients; price and cost information; and the default GL accounts and subac<br>counts to be used for transactions with the items. See also inventory item, ware<br>house, general ledger, and account.                                                                  |
| notification template | An email template with variables denoting values in an employee or contact<br>record. When the email is sent, the system replaces variables with values from<br>the database record associated with each addressee for email personalization.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

<span id="page-200-5"></span><span id="page-200-4"></span><span id="page-200-3"></span><span id="page-200-2"></span><span id="page-200-1"></span><span id="page-200-0"></span>

| numbering sequence | A set of rules the system uses to generate the next unique identifier when you<br>create a new object of certain type (such as a batch). provides a number of<br>predefined numbering sequences you can use. A numbering sequence may<br>have subsequences. If one numbering sequence is used for multiple object<br>types, all the objects get numbers according to the order in which they were<br>created, so successive numbers can be assigned to objects of different types.<br>See also batch.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| O                  |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| overdue charges    | Charges calculated on open Accounts Receivable items that are past due.<br>Acumatica ERP calculates overdue charges and displays them on customer<br>statements. You can configure these charges to be compound charges<br>(charges calculated on charges) or not. Overdue charges are based on terms<br>that provide a schedule for payment. See also accounts receivable and cus<br>tomer statement.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| P                  |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| payment method     | A way in which customers pay for goods they purchase from your organization.<br>For each payment method, you can use a number of predefined elements: de<br>fine the element names as you want them to appear on the interface, and set<br>up input validation for these elements (input masks or regular expressions).<br>Payment methods are based on the following general means of payment:<br>credit cards, gi certificates, purchase orders, cash cards, and custom meth<br>ods. See also customer and input mask.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| PI cycle           | The physical inventory cycle assigned to the stock item. PI cycles are used to<br>arrange the items into groups for periodic counting. For more details on using<br>PI cycles, see Planning for Physical Inventory. See also stock item.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| posting class      | A group of items that defines the default account to be used and the rules for<br>composing the default subaccount for transactions with the applicable inven<br>tory items. Accounts and subaccounts for transactions can be obtained from<br>the following sources: inventory item, warehouse, or posting class. See also<br>combined subaccount, Inventory, account, subaccount, combined subaccount,<br>warehouse, and inventory item.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| prepayment         | A document that represents amounts paid in advance for future purchases. A<br>vendor's request for prepayment is processed as follows: You use the Checks<br>and Payments (AP302000) form to enter the prepayment. Then the prepay<br>ment is paid in full by an AP check in the same currency as the default cash<br>account. If the payment method associated with the default cash account re<br>quires printing a check, print it and release the AP check, which changes its<br>status to Closed and creates a payment of the Prepayment type with the refer<br>ence number of the original prepayment request. After that, you can apply the<br>prepayment to bills and adjustments. See also accounts payable. |
| price list         | A list of sales prices that is set for goods sold in a specific currency, offered to<br>customers of a particular customer price class, and specified with respect to<br>various units of measure available for the items. In Acumatica ERP, you can<br>maintain multiple price lists. See also sales price, customer, and customer price<br>class.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

<span id="page-201-3"></span><span id="page-201-2"></span><span id="page-201-1"></span><span id="page-201-0"></span>

| purchase orders           | A functional area of Acumatica ERP that provides functionality for efficient<br>management of your company's supply chain and optimization of the cost of<br>acquiring materials or services.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|---------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| purchase requisitions     | A functional area of Acumatica ERP with forms you can use to streamline and<br>customize the process of requesting needed items. You can request goods and<br>services, approve requests, and prevent cost overruns.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| R                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| reason code               | A code used to provide additional information regarding transactions in the<br>system. When you configure a reason code on the Reason Codes (CS211000)<br>form, you can specify whether this code is used for inventory and if so, how it<br>is used. By using inventory-related reason codes, you can post transactions re<br>lated to direct inventory operations (such as receipts, issues, transfers, adjust<br>ments, and physical inventory counts) to specific accounts and assign particu<br>lar subaccounts to them for more detailed reporting. See also reason code, In<br>ventory, account, and subaccount.                                                                                                           |
| reconciliation            | The process of matching the cash transactions recorded in Acumatica ERP<br>against those presented on a bank statement. Theoretically, the balance of<br>the cash account associated with the bank should reconcile to the balance<br>of the bank statement, but there may be some discrepancy between account<br>balances. The goal of reconciliation is to find discrepancies and determine<br>whether each is due to entry errors or timing. In Acumatica ERP, you mark doc<br>uments as cleared as you receive preliminary information from the bank. Lat<br>er, when you have received the bank statement, you reconcile transactions<br>with the bank statement.                                                            |
| recurring GL transactions | GL transactions that repeat regularly. To automate the entering of recurring<br>transactions, such as depreciation transactions, Acumatica ERP gives you the<br>ability to create schedules for them. A schedule defines how many times and<br>how often specific batches should be repeated. One batch or multiple batches<br>can be assigned to a schedule as long as they have the Balanced status. Once<br>a batch is assigned to a schedule, its status changes to Scheduled. To create<br>schedules, use the Recurring Transactions (GL203500) form. See also schedule<br>and batch.                                                                                                                                        |
| replenishment policy      | Settings that define how automatic replenishment for the inventory item is<br>initiated, as well as its source, quantity, and time intervals, including low sea<br>sons, during which replenishment is initiated in smaller quantities. See also in<br>ventory item.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| restriction group         | A set of objects (such as users, accounts, and subaccounts) of two or more<br>types created to, if the group includes users, restrict users' access to only ob<br>jects in the same group; if the group doesn't include users, the restriction<br>group relates its objects in a way that limits their use. For instance, one restric<br>tion group may include two users and a number of special-use accounts that<br>only these two users can update, and another restriction group may include<br>several GL expense accounts and a subaccount that should be used only with<br>these particular accounts. If a restriction group is defined as inverse, the ob<br>jects in the group instead cannot be used with one another. |

<span id="page-202-6"></span><span id="page-202-5"></span><span id="page-202-4"></span><span id="page-202-3"></span><span id="page-202-2"></span><span id="page-202-1"></span><span id="page-202-0"></span>

| Retained Earnings account | A special system-maintained accounts that is of the Liability type and must be<br>created before any actual data is entered. The Retained Earnings account ac<br>cumulates the company's net income (or loss) after the dividends have been<br>paid. Retained earnings are summarized over the years since the first year of<br>company operations.
